questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The scientific study of the Loch Ness Monster
How to draw a unicorn and other magical animals
Why unicorns are popular again, from shops to politics
The history of white horses in British art
questions.why: Neil says unicorns are popping up everywhere, even in politics, and asks why.

questions.q: Why doesn't Rob say the answer to the quiz question at first?
options: He has no idea what the answer is
He already knows it from an earlier programme
He wants to guess later, after hearing some clues
Neil tells him not to say it until the end
questions.why: He says it was the topic of a programme in 2008, so he'll keep it to himself.

questions.q: Where have unicorns been appearing recently?
options: Only in children's books and fairy tales
In zoos and wildlife parks around Scotland
In old paintings in national museums
On T-shirts, in films, as toys and in politics
questions.why: Neil lists T-shirts, movies, toys and political conversations.

questions.q: Why did people use to drink from unicorn horn cups, according to Natalie Lawrence?
options: To protect themselves from poison
To become stronger
Because they were very beautiful
To show they were rich
questions.why: She says they drank from them 'to prevent themselves getting poisoned'.

questions.q: When were the original unicorn stories developed?
options: In the last few years, on social media
When people believed magic was real
During a long war between two kingdoms
In the 2008 programme about horses
questions.why: She says they were developed 'in a time when magic actually existed in the world'.

questions.q: Why does Neil think unicorns are popular now?
options: People want a bit of magic in their lives
They are cheap to make and easy to sell
Scientists say they have found a real one
Children demand them for every birthday
questions.why: He says people seem to be looking for a bit of magic in their lives.

questions.q: What does 'unicorn' mean in UK politics?
options: A very popular politician who wins elections
A special new law that everyone agrees with
A plan that is unrealistic and can't work
A national symbol of the UK and Scotland
questions.why: Neil says it's a negative comment: a fantasy idea with no chance of working.

questions.q: Why does Neil mention the army when explaining 'deploy'?
options: The army uses the unicorn as a symbol on its flags
Politicians want to send the army to deal with it
Unicorns were used as symbols in old wars
The word is used as if politics were a war
questions.why: He compares deploying the army with deploying the word 'unicorn' in the political conflict.
